subject: Bundle fit assessment and seat-smoothing request - Medisync packaging
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medisync.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Derek Holt <derek.holt@medisync.io>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial packaging question: expected throughput + plan fit

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: MediSync is evaluating Redwood to power patient-summary generation (chat) and embeddings for search. Our primary constraints are predictable throughput during business hours and minimizing per-token cost at scale. Rough numbers: ~3M tokens/day today, peak concurrent chat requests ~180 RPS (short sequences), embeddings workload bursts up to ~400/s.

Questions:
- Which Redwood plan best maps to our mix (tiered seats vs throughput buckets vs Dedicated)?
- How do upgrades/downgrades work mid-quarter (proration, credits)?
- Can you confirm what feature-bundles are included (model switching, KV prefix caching, streaming)?
- Any standard commitment discounts for 6/12 month terms?

I attached a small usage sample for reference (medisync-usage-sample.csv). Happy to do a 30-minute call if that helps. 

Best,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
VP, Product
MediSync

Attachments:
- medisync-usage-sample.csv (text/csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medisync.io>
Cc: Derek Holt <derek.holt@medisync.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial packaging question: expected throughput + plan fit

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detail and the sample; that helps a lot. Quick answers up front and then a few next steps:

- Short answer: Based on the mix you described, we'd usually recommend either (A) a Scale plan with throughput buckets + seat smoothing for predictable daytime peaks, or (B) Redwood Dedicated if you want strict isolation and the lowest unit cost for sustained throughput.
- Upgrades/downgrades: pro-rated within the billing period. We support step-downs at quarter boundaries with a short grace period; logistics depend on committed vs metered billing.
- Feature bundles: caching (prefix/KV), model variant switching (policy-limited), streaming, and tracing are included in Scale; Dedicated adds priority routing and custom autoscale rules.
- Commit discounts: standard is ~10–15% for 12-month commits at Scale; Dedicated has deeper tiers starting at ~12% for mid commits.

Can Ben (AE) and Priya (Solutions) jump in with a tailored options email? If MediSync prefers, we can sketch 2–3 concrete pricing packages and a DocuSign-ready proposal.

I attached a quick overview of pack options.

Cheers,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-pack-options.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Medisync packaging — options to propose

Ben/Priya — summarizing Samantha's ask and the quick recommendation so we can finalize an offer. MediSync: ~3M tokens/day, 180 RPS chat peaks, embeddings bursts to 400/s. Region: US; security requirements: SOC2 (they flagged procurement later).

Option sketches (aiming to be clear and negotiable):
1) Scale Tier (best fit): 200k tokens/min throughput bucket w/ seat smoothing (daytime burst protection), includes caching + 3 model variant switches/month. Base list: $45k/mo; 12mo commit -> 12% discount.
2) High-Throughput Scale (discount for volume): 500k tokens/min bucket w/ pref routing, includes caching, streaming, priority support. Base list: $95k/mo; 12mo commit -> 15% discount.
3) Dedicated (pricey but lowest per-token): Dedicated GPU pods, SLA 99.9, custom autoscale. Baseline: $140k/mo; 12mo commit -> 18% discount.

Negotiation levers: commit length, up-front payment, limited model-switch allowance, pilot credits, quantization/packing advice to reduce tokens.

Target ask: can we offer a 15% effective discount with a 9–12 month commit and a pilot credit of $20k? Need to know your comfort level on model-switch limits (Samantha asked about "unlimited" — we should cap or meter heavy churn).

Pls advise and I can draft a proposal for Sam.

—Kim

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Medisync packaging — options to propose

Agree with the framing. Proposed firm options to present to MediSync (we can tune numbers once they confirm tokens/day):

A — Scale Starter (conservative): $40k/mo list; 12 mo commit -> 10% discount. Seat smoothing add-on $6k/mo. Includes 3 model variant changes/month, caching, streaming.
B — Scale Plus (recommended): $85k/mo list; 12 mo commit -> 15% discount; includes seat smoothing, priority support, and 5 model variant changes/month. Offer a $15k pilot credit (applied to first invoice) if they sign within 21 days.
C — Dedicated Intro (for predictable high throughput): $125k/mo list; 12 mo commit -> 18% discount; includes SLA, dedicated routing, unlimited support. For dedicated we ask for a 3-yr optional extension clause for deeper discounts.

Counter on "unlimited model switching": we should say model switching is included with reasonable use (5/month) — beyond that charge at $200/change.

I'll attach a draft proposal PDF and a pricing worksheet. If you want, we can pre-draft DocuSign and include a PO template.

Regards,
Ben

Attachments:
- proposal-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medisync.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Derek Holt <derek.holt@medisync.io>, procurement@medisync.io
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Bundle fit assessment and seat-smoothing request - Medisync packaging

Kimberly/Ben — thanks for the clear options. A few procurement questions before we schedule an exec review:

1) Can you provide final pricing with line items (list vs discounted) and a sample invoice?
2) How precisely does seat-smoothing billing look — how are bursts billed when they exceed the bucket?
3) SOC2 + data residency: do you have certs and a standard attestation we can include in the SOW?
4) Competitive pushback: another vendor has offered a 20% discount on a similar 12mo commit. Can Redwood match 20% or offer alternative concessions (e.g., longer pilot credits, favorable SLA terms)?
5) Regarding model switching: unlimited is preferred on our side — if you cap changes, will you commit to a fast self-serve model swap tool or reduced change fees?

If you can send a DocuSign draft, procurement will review with Derek and legal next week.

Best,
Samantha

On Mon, Feb 15, 2027 at 10:10 AM Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Agree with the framing... (quoted for context)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Feb 2027 10:58:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Medisync procurement negotiation - suggested counter

Ben/Priya — procurement pushed for 20% citing a competitor. My recommended counter:

- Offer: Scale Plus at $85k/mo list with a 12-mo commit and 18% discount (effective $69,700/mo). Include $20k pilot credit, 5 model variant changes/month free, and a self-serve model-switching tool availability within 30 days. Seat-smoothing add-on included.
- For SOC2/data residency: attach our SOC2 report and standard attestation; add a 30-day SOW appendix for residency controls (we can route to Security for an addendum).
- If they insist on 20%, trade: 20% only for a 24-mo commit OR 12-mo + 25% upfront payment.

I think this is a defensible middle ground and preserves margin while giving them the tooling they asked for. Ben — can you prepare the DocuSign with these terms (I'll approve). Priya — please confirm the timeline to have the self-serve model switch available and whether we need legal to carve anything for the change fee.

—Kim

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@medisync.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Derek Holt <derek.holt@medisync.io>, procurement@medisync.io
Date: Thu, 17 Feb 2027 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Bundle fit assessment and seat-smoothing request - Medisync packaging

Kim/Ben — thank you. The counter looks reasonable. We can accept the Scale Plus with 18% discount for a 12-month term plus the $20k pilot credit and 5 model switches/month. Procurement would prefer the 18% be applied across invoices rather than taken as a prepayment.

Next steps: please send the DocuSign with the final SOW (include SOC2 attestation and the model-switch SLA language). Derek will loop legal and procurement for a quick review; if everything looks good, we aim to sign within 7 business days.

I'll share a PO template once DocuSign is live.

Thanks,
Samantha
